lines.line: Motivation or discipline? Almost half who planned to exercise didn't do it.
lines.quote: In 10 studies of 3,899 people, almost half of those who intended to exercise (46%) did not follow through. Just 2% of everyone studied exercised without having intended to.
lines.source: Rhodes RE, de Bruijn GJ. How big is the physical activity intention-behaviour gap? A meta-analysis using the action control framework. British Journal of Health Psychology, 2013, 18(2):296-309. doi:10.1111/bjhp.12032. Systematic review and meta-analysis, 10 studies, N = 3,899; activity judged against public-health guideline levels.

lines.line: An old fable book: good goals don't come by wishing. Get up!
lines.quote: Worthy ends come not by wishing. Wouldst thou? Up, and win it, then! While the hungry lion slumbers, not a deer comes to his den.
lines.source: Hitopadesha, Introduction (Prastavika), verse 36 (numbering of the sanskritdocuments.org text, transliterated by J. Janbrz, proofread by Avinash). English tr. Edwin Arnold, The Book of Good Counsels, 1861, as reprinted in Epiphanius Wilson (ed.), Hindu Literature, 1900 (Project Gutenberg #13268). Sanskrit checked at https://sanskritdocuments.org/~sanskrit/doc_trial/fortransfer/hitopadesha.itx

lines.line: Sparks are real: Murakami's idea came suddenly. Then he wrote every night.
lines.quote: In that instant, for no reason and based on no grounds whatsoever, it suddenly struck me: I think I can write a novel. ... Each night after that, when I got home late from work, I sat at my kitchen table and wrote.
lines.source: Haruki Murakami, 'The Birth of My Kitchen-Table Fiction', introduction to Hear the Wind Sing and Pinball, 1973 (Wind/Pinball), tr. Ted Goossen (Harvill Secker / Knopf, 2015), pp. viii-ix (quoted lines on p. ix; publisher's sample PDF)

lines.line: Zig Ziglar: motivation doesn't last. Neither does a bath. Take both regularly.
lines.quote: Of course motivation is not permanent. But then, neither is bathing; but it is something you should do on a regular basis.
lines.source: Zig Ziglar, Raising Positive Kids in a Negative World (Nashville: Oliver Nelson, 1985). He gives it as 'My answer' when told that, in other words, 'motivation is not permanent.'

lines.line: No spark yet? Stravinsky: just as eating brings appetite, work brings inspiration.
lines.quote: The uninitiated imagine that one must await inspiration in order to create. That is a mistake. ... Just as appetite comes by eating, so work brings inspiration, if inspiration is not discernible at the beginning.
lines.source: Igor Stravinsky, An Autobiography (Simon & Schuster, 1936, translator not named; Norton Library reprint 1962), Part Two 'Composer and Performer', closing pages, p. 174 (Norton ed.); French original Chroniques de ma vie, 1935

lines.line: Novelist Trollope trusted sticky wax on his chair more than inspiration.
lines.quote: I was once told that the surest aid to the writing of a book was a piece of cobbler's wax on my chair. I certainly believe in the cobbler's wax much more than the inspiration.
lines.source: Anthony Trollope, An Autobiography (1883), Chapter VII

lines.line: Low energy? In 158 studies, one cardio workout went with more energy.
lines.quote: A meta-analysis of 158 studies (13,101 participants, 1979-2005) found that after one bout of aerobic exercise, self-reported energetic, positive feeling rose by about half a standard deviation (d = .47), and the lift seemed to last at least 30 minutes. Effects were consistently positive even when people started out feeling less upbeat than average. In control conditions, this feeling dipped slightly (d = -.17).
lines.source: Reed J, Ones DS. The effect of acute aerobic exercise on positive activated affect: A meta-analysis. Psychology of Sport and Exercise 7(5):477-514, September 2006. DOI 10.1016/j.psychsport.2005.11.003.

lines.line: Rabbi Tarfon: you needn't finish the work, but you can't skip it.
lines.credit: Rabbi Tarfon · Pirkei Avot 2:16, tr. Kulp
lines.quote: It is not your duty to finish the work, but neither are you at liberty to neglect it.
lines.source: Mishnah, Pirkei Avot 2:16 (Sefaria numbering; some editions number it differently), tr. Joshua Kulp, Mishnah Yomit (on Sefaria, CC-BY). Older public-domain tr. Charles Taylor, Sayings of the Jewish Fathers, 2nd ed., Cambridge, 1897: 'It is not for thee to finish the work, nor art thou free to desist therefrom.' Text read through Sefaria's API: https://www.sefaria.org/api/v3/texts/Pirkei_Avot.2.16

lines.line: The Gita: each time the restless mind wanders off, bring it back.
lines.quote: As often as the wavering and unsteady mind goeth forth, so often reining it in, let him bring it under the control of the Self.
lines.source: Bhagavad Gita 6.26, tr. Annie Besant, The Bhagavad-Gita or The Lord's Song, 4th ed., G. A. Natesan, Madras, 1922 (Wikisource proofread transcription; Index: Bhagavad Gita - Annie Besant 4th edition.djvu).

lines.line: Krishnamacharya: yoga's benefits come only with daily practice, same time, same place.
lines.quote: ...there is no doubt that until yogabhyasa is done with the same attitude, practised every day at the same prescribed time and place, one will not obtain the expected benefits of the action.
lines.source: T. Krishnamacharya, Yoga Makaranda, Part 1, ch. 1 'Introduction', sec. 1.1 'Why should yogabhyasa be done', p. 8. Written in Kannada (Kannada edition 1934); Tamil tr. C. M. V. Krishnamacharya, 1938; English tr. Lakshmi Ranganathan and Nandini Ranganathan (translators' note dated 15 Oct 2006).

lines.line: Fast horse or slow? Xunzi: the slow one, never quitting, gets there.
lines.quote: A fine horse cannot cover ten paces in one leap; a slow horse pulling for ten days gets there: the achievement lies in not giving up. Carve and give up, and even rotten wood won't break; carve and don't give up, and metal and stone can be engraved.
lines.source: Xunzi, ch. 1 'Encouraging Learning' (勸學), Chinese text with the Tang-dynasty commentary of Yang Liang (zh.wikisource 荀子/勸學篇). Yang Liang glosses 鍥，刻也 ('鍥 means to carve'). Older English: Homer H. Dubs, The Works of Hsüntze, 1928, which renders 鍥 as 'sickle' (a mistranslation) and 十步 as 'a thousand paces'.

lines.line: Audiobooks only at the gym: 51% more visits, then the boost shrank.
lines.quote: 226 students, faculty and staff at a US university were randomly assigned. Those who could listen to their page-turner audiobooks only at the gym went 51% more often at first, but the boost shrank over time, especially after the Thanksgiving break.
lines.source: Milkman KL, Minson JA, Volpp KGM. Holding the Hunger Games hostage at the gym: An evaluation of temptation bundling. Management Science, 2014, 60(2):283-299. doi:10.1287/mnsc.2013.1784. Randomized field experiment, N = 226 (75 full, 75 intermediate, 76 control), 86% undergraduates, recruited September 2011, about 9-10 weeks. The main title names a novel series; keep it off slides.

lines.line: What lasts? Habits are likely to keep going after motivation fades.
lines.quote: Once initiation of the action is 'transferred' to external cues, dependence on conscious attention or motivational processes is reduced. Therefore habits are likely to persist even after conscious motivation or interest dissipates.
lines.source: Gardner B, Lally P, Wardle J. Making health habitual: the psychology of 'habit-formation' and general practice. British Journal of General Practice, 2012 Dec, 62(605):664-666. doi:10.3399/bjgp12X659466.

lines.line: Estimated: a morning stretch becomes automatic in about 106 days, evening 154.
lines.quote: 48 students tried to make one stretch a habit over 90 days, randomly assigned to do it on waking or before bed. Extending their learning curves, the researchers estimated the morning group would reach automaticity sooner (about 106 days) than the evening group (about 154 days).
lines.source: Fournier M, d'Arripe-Longueville F, Rovere C, Easthope CS, Schwabe L, El Methni J, Radel R. Effects of circadian cortisol on the development of a health habit. Health Psychology, 2017, 36(11):1059-1064. doi:10.1037/hea0000510.

lines.line: Motivation matters too: people who enjoyed exercise tended to keep doing it.
lines.quote: A systematic review of 66 studies found a trend: enjoying exercise for its own sake (intrinsic motivation) better predicted sticking with it long-term, while doing it because you value its benefits better predicted starting.
lines.source: Teixeira PJ, Carraça EV, Markland D, Silva MN, Ryan RM. Exercise, physical activity, and self-determination theory: A systematic review. International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity 9:78, 2012. DOI 10.1186/1479-5868-9-78.

lines.line: Baseball's Cal Ripken came ready to play: 2,632 games in a row.
lines.quote: My thought was that my job was to come to the ballpark ready to play to meet the challenges of today, and if the manager chose me then I played.
lines.source: Cal Ripken Jr. interviewed in Dante Ciampaglia, 'Cal Ripken Looks Back on The Streak', SI Kids, 20 Sept 2013. Streak facts from the Smithsonian 'Great Americans' medal page

lines.line: Motivation or discipline? A Japanese saying: continuing is power.
lines.quote: Continuing is power.
lines.source: Digital Daijisen (Shogakukan), entry 継続は力なり, on Kotobank. Origin discussion: HugKum (Shogakukan), https://hugkum.sho.jp/528632

lines.line: Vivekananda: character is repeated habits, and only repeated habits can reshape it.
lines.quote: Character is repeated habits, and repeated habits alone can reform character.
lines.source: Swami Vivekananda, Raja Yoga (London: Longmans, Green, 1896), commentary on Yoga Aphorisms I.12; p. 112 in the 1907 9th impression (Wellcome Library scan).
lines.credit_note: Shortened 22 Oct so it fits one line. Same source: Raja Yoga (1896), commentary on Yoga Sutra I.12.

lines.line: Patanjali's word for practice is abhyasa: repeated effort to steady the mind.
lines.quote: Practice (abhyāsa) is [repeated] exertion to the end that [the mind-stuff] shall have permanence in this [restricted state]. [Vyasa:] Practice is an effort (prayatna) ... a persevering struggle.
lines.source: Yoga Sutra 1.13 with Vyasa's Yoga-bhashya, tr. James Haughton Woods, The Yoga-System of Patanjali, Harvard Oriental Series vol. 17, Harvard University Press, 1914, pp. 34-35.

lines.line: Pattabhi Jois put it simply: do your practice, and all is coming.
lines.credit: Pattabhi Jois · in Miele, Astanga Yoga, 1996
lines.quote: This, together with the belief in my sound philosophy, "Do your practice and all is coming" will greatly reward the efforts of my students.
lines.source: Signed message 'With Blessings, Sri K. Pattabhi Jois' printed at the front of Lino Miele, Astanga Yoga, published by Lino Miele, Rome; copyright 1996 by Angelo Michele Miele. The edition list reads 1st 1994, 2nd 1996, up to 8th 2007; the scan opened is an 8th-edition (2007) printing.
